grades.reason: Discusses fork, execution, and child termination, but not memory sharing or copy-on-write isolation.

grades.quote:
All it needs to do is map all the virtual pages to the same physical page frame and mark them as read-only.

In itself, this technique of sharing a page frame of zeros doesn’t address the situation where a process writes into one of its zeroed pages. However, that situation can be handled using a variant of the COW technique mentioned in Section 6.2.2. When the MMU interrupts the processor due to a write into the read-only page of zeros, the operating system can update the mapping for that one page to refer to a separate read/write page frame of zeros and then resume the process.
grades.reason: Explains read-only sharing and private writable remapping on a write fault, but for zero pages rather than parent-child fork mappings.
Mentions COW in a scheduling exercise but provides no explanation of its isolation mechanism.

grades.quote: For example, in fork, the parent writes the child’s user memory pages, and the child (a different thread, perhaps on a different CPU) reads those pages; no lock explicitly protects those pages. This is not strictly a locking problem, since the child doesn’t start executing until after the parent has finished writing.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary background on fork memory initialization and ordering, but does not explain COW sharing or protection against subsequent writes.
